correctness.rationale: Zero GMRES(2) correction is optimal exactly when r^T Mr=r^T M²r=0. Writing Q=x²+y²+z² and P=y(ux+vz), normal equations give Q+P=0, Q+2P+uvxz=0, so Q=uvxz>0 and xz>0. Normalize xz=1, t=x²>0, eliminate y to obtain exactly uv=G_{v/u}(t), with converse. The function diverges at both ends and attains a positive minimum, proving iff. Q>x²+z²≥2xz implies threshold>2; test t=1 gives bound≤2+2rho/(rho²+rho+1)≤8/3; the balanced factorization proves 8/3. Exact radical example u=(5+sqrt5)/(2sqrt2), v=(5-sqrt5)/(2sqrt2), r=(1,-1/sqrt2,1) satisfies both normal equations. The TGA subspace span{r,Mr} gives the same first-cycle minimum; unaccelerated (I-M)^3=0. Five independent symbolic assertions corroborated critical identities, with analytic proof for all weights.

originality.rationale: The known standard-Jordan (equal-superdiagonal) GMRES theory is explicitly excluded from novelty. The ratio-dependent Euclidean frontier for fixed unequal upper links, and same-product reversal, are not implied by equal-link bounds: diagonal similarity is nonunitary. A paper constructing some matrices with prescribed stagnation cannot solve the fixed pair (u,v) classification. The originating two-grid paper supplies algorithmic context but its full technical version was inaccessible; this remains a qualified best-knowledge assessment.

final_claim: For M_{u,v}=I+u E12+v E23 with u,v>0, some nonzero real residual exhibits complete Euclidean GMRES(2) stagnation iff uv >= min_{t>0} (t^2+1)(t+rho)^2/[t(t^2+rho*t+rho^2)], rho=v/u. The attained threshold lies in (2,8/3], equals 8/3 exactly at rho=1, tends to 2 for extreme ratios, and also governs the specified first TGA(1;1,0) two-grid cycle. A same-product 5/2 anisotropic example stalls but its balanced equal-link counterpart always improves.
limitations: Real exact arithmetic, dimension 3, u,v strictly positive, Euclidean residual, specified first TGA cycle.
No general GMRES iteration-count stability, floating-point guarantee, or large-n extension.
